positions.as_written: Assess the effusion, since a recurrent activity related effusion is the common finding when the result is not holding.
Measure the range, recording any restriction, because stiffness after cartilage surgery is common.
Assess the painful arc, since a treated lesion is loaded at a particular flexion angle.
Assess the alignment, because the load that produced the lesion has not changed unless it was corrected.
Assess function, because the patient's judgement of the result is functional rather than structural.
Repair tissue tolerates less load than the cartilage it replaces.
Repair tissue quality determines the durability and is invisible to the examination, so the clinical result and the structural one can diverge for years.
Repair tissue quality is invisible to the examination.
